Title: Sacrorum Conciliorum nova et amplissima collectio, cujus Joannes Dominicus Mansi et post ipsius mortem Florentinus et Venetus editores priores triginta unum tomos ediderunt, nunc autem continuata et Deo favente absoluta; Tomus trigesimus quintus, in quo continentur reliqui textus ab anno MCDXIV ad annum MDCCXXIV pertinentes
Creator: Joannes Dominicus Mansi; the texts taken from his Supplement to Coleti's collection, vols. V-VI
Publisher: Paris and Leipzig: H. Welter, 1902 (facsimile reproduction by Carl Reinecke, Berlin, 250 copies)
Publication Date: 1902
Rights: Public Domain (published 1902, more than 95 years ago; public domain by date under the project's rolling rule; the item carries no rights field, so the date rule alone applies)
Language: lat
Source: Internet Archive item sacrorumconcilio0035joan (https://archive.org/details/sacrorumconcilio0035joan), the item's own sacrorumconcilio0035joan_djvu.txt full-text OCR derivative; contributing library per the item metadata: Internet Archive; host metadata date: 1901. Fetched directly (curl/urllib, raw bytes) by the Library thread (Era VIII pass), 2026-10-23. sha256 of the raw fetched bytes: 5ccb5218b437c83ecbe99cf96a966cf0b8ab53a0457ef22ce2468454dd9195ee.
Provenance note: Header prepended by the Library thread; nothing else altered, no OCR error corrected, nothing retyped. Internet Archive's own scan (Cebu scanning centre, 2026) of the Welter facsimile; the host dates it 1901, the title page 1902. The facsimile reprints the texts of Mansi's Supplement as its own notice on the title page says. Two-column Latin with long s kept and running heads.
Content note: Supplementary conciliar texts from 1414 to 1724. For this entry the core is the full acts of the Synodus provincialis Ruthenorum habita in civitate Zamosciae anno 1720 (columns 1437-1538): the metropolitan's dedication to Benedict XIII, the papal confirmation, the decrees of Propaganda and of the Congregation of the Council, the nuncio Grimaldi's address to the synod, the professions of faith of all present, Metropolitan Leo Kiszka's letters, and the synod's decrees. The rest of the volume carries other supplements (Constance, Florence, Lateran V and later synods).
